messages.subject: bilat.symmetry() error?
parts:
Hi All!


I was using the bilat.symmetry() function with the new geomorph 3.0.4 and came by what I believe are a couple of bugs and wanted to ask for some help.


First of all, I run the analisis and the code works, but then when I try to retrieve the asymmetic component of shape variation via "bilat.symmetry$asym.shape" what I get is NULL in the command console. I find this strange since I am able to retrieve the fluctuating asymmetry component "bilat.symmetry$FA.component", so the function must have computed an asymmetric shape variation component. Or is it that matching symmetry gives a result for "bilat.symmetry$asym.shape" and when you have object symmetry you only retrieve the "bilat.symmetry$FA.component"?? I would appreciate it if someone could clear this up for me, I have object symmetry.


I also wanted to plot the results, but the x-axis of the plots always uses what is labeled as "Index" no matter what component I use. So I cannot see a proper scatter of the individuals in the shared morphospace. I am not very good with the plot() function so maybe I am missing out on how to do this. Can someone help me out? I was using this line of code:


x11(); plot(bilat.symmetry$FA.component, warpgrids = TRUE, mesh = NULL)




Best wishes,

Javier

messages.author: 2fc03d53bc863e8d
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: bilat.symmetry() error?
parts:
That NULL result may be due to the spelling of "asymm". The asymmetric shape component is named "asymm.shape" not "asym.shape" (although the manual does spell it as "asym.shape" when it gives the values of the function).
In your plot command, I'm not sure what you called the output of the bilat.symmetry function. Say you called it symData; to plot all the results, you'd use plot(symData). If you want to plot the superimposed coordinates of the asymmetric component, you could use
plotAllSpecimens(symData$asymm.shape)

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: bilat.symmetry() error?
parts:
That is certainly the issue.  I’m not sure how it passed by the CRAN check that matches output names in Rd and R files, but it is a typo in the help file.  Alas, I have updated the typo on Github, so a fresh download of geomorph will have “asymm.shape” correctly spelled in the help file.

As a tip when something like this happens again, at least in R Studio, if one types, e.g., symData$, a list should appear, which gets smaller as one keeps typing.  Selecting an object from the list guarantees a match to the objects that are available.  R does not return an error when one requests an object that does not exist; it returns NULL.  Therefore, I often start typing the object after “$” that I want and then select it, having R fill in the remainder of characters, so that I make sure not to type the wrong word.

Cheers
Mike

parts:
Hi guys,


Thank you, Mike, Miriam, and Emma, for the fast response! I'm not used to that and I appreciate it.


The problem with the asymmetric component bilat.symmetry$asymm.shape was indeed the extra "m". I was following the help section of the function where it is written with only one. Sometimes I write really fast so I don't see the autocomplete of R... also I normally prefer to choose my own stuff and ignore or remove autocomplete entirely from my software. With the extra "m" I get the shape component correctly now.


I'm still getting used to the plotting in R though. When I use the plot() function with no extra arguments I get this error that makes reference to the xlabel, which I believe means that there are many xlabels to choose from and I have to specify more:

>  FA<-bilat.symmetry(A=GPAFA,ind=ids,object.sym=T,land.pairs=pairs,RRPP=T,iter=999)

> x11(); plot(FA)
Error in plot3d.default(M1, type = "s", col = gP$pt.bg, size = gP$pt.size,  : 
  formal argument "xlab" matched by multiple actual arguments

But if I use this line of code like Miriam said I do get the dispersion graph of the 3D LM configurations:
>  x11(); plotAllSpecimens(FA$asymm.shape)

Now I wanted to plot the "bilat.symmetry$FA.component" fluctuating asymmetry component as a vector from the consensus configuration. I used this code and get the 3D LM configuration, but I do not know how to command the function to make the vectors representing the LM deviations from the mean:

>  x11(); plotAllSpecimens(FA$FA.component, mean=T,links=NULL)

I also don't get the mean configuration in the plot. Is this because I performed the GPA before running the bilat.symmetry() function?

How can I indicate the plotAllSpecimens() function to represent the fluctuating asymmetry component as vectors from the mean in R in this situation?

All help is appreciated, thank you all!



Best wishes,

Javier
